x-m-h2-01.title: Find di line wey logarithm equation solution get problem

x-m-h2-01.material: Minho solve log₂(x−1) + log₂(x−3) = 3 and answer, ‘Solutions na x=5 and x=−1, two of dem.’ Read am as ‘log base 2 of (x minus 1) plus log base 2 of (x minus 3) equals 3’.

x-m-h2-01.s.s1.line.5: So solutions na x = 5 and x = −1, two of dem.

If x=5, log₂4 + log₂2 = 2+1 = 3, so e work. So only solution na x=5.
x-m-h2-01.s.s2.prompt: Tell Minho correct solution and reason. Include problem wey happen if x=−1 enter original equation.
x-m-h2-01.s.s2.hint.0: Read and check why expression change at each line.

x-m-h2-01.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You use argument value explain why x=−1 no fit be solution?
x-m-h2-01.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You say which condition needed before expression change?
x-m-h2-01.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You put x=5 inside original equation and check say e work?
x-m-h2-01.s.s2.model.0: Only solution na x=5. If I put x=−1, argument negative like log₂(−2), so e no define. So na only 5, wey satisfy argument condition x>3, be solution.
x-m-h2-01.s.s2.model.1: When you solve equation, arguments must always positive. x−1>0 and x−3>0, so x>3 needed; x=−1 no dey inside range, so remove am. Answer na x=5.

x-m-h2-04.title: How many triangles fit make from two sides and one angle?
x-m-h2-04.goal: Test the general claim “always get two” with specific values, and explain with reasons which cases no follow am.
x-m-h2-04.material: For triangle ABC, ∠A=60° and side BC length na a=7. When length b of side CA dey given, you fit fix length c of side AB and make triangle. (a, b, c na sides opposite ∠A, ∠B, ∠C. cos60°=1/2.) Gaeun talk say, “If b bigger than 7, dem always make two such triangles.”
x-m-h2-04.thinking.0: Make cases wey satisfy conditions yourself
x-m-h2-04.thinking.1: Choose values wey disprove the claim
x-m-h2-04.prereq.0: Trigonometric ratios and relationship between sides and angles for triangle
x-m-h2-04.prereq.1: Number of roots for quadratic equation
x-m-h2-04.s.s1.prompt: Make triangles wey fit conditions when b=8. Find two different possible lengths c for side AB.
x-m-h2-04.s.s1.hint.0: Put a=7, b=8, cos60°=1/2 inside cosine rule and write equation for c.
x-m-h2-04.s.s1.hint.1: Choose all solutions for that equation wey fit serve as side length.
x-m-h2-04.s.s1.fail.c2: Equation wey you get when you put a=7, b=8 inside cosine rule a²=b²+c²−2bc·cos60° no hold.
x-m-h2-04.s.s1.explain: From 49=64+c²−8c, c²−8c+15=0, (c−3)(c−5)=0, so c=3 or 5. Both values positive, so two triangles fit make.
x-m-h2-04.s.s2.prompt: Choose all b values wey fit disprove Gaeun statement (if b bigger than 7, always get two triangles). For each b, set up equation for c the same way.
x-m-h2-04.s.s2.hint.0: For each b, rearrange 49=b²+c²−bc as quadratic in c.
x-m-h2-04.s.s2.hint.1: Use discriminant check whether rearranged equation get real roots, and check whether value dey inside condition b>7 too.
x-m-h2-04.s.s2.r.a: E become c²−10c+51=0, wey no get real roots. This na case where no triangle fit make at all.
x-m-h2-04.s.s2.r.b: b=5 dey outside condition “b bigger than 7,” so e no disprove Gaeun statement.
x-m-h2-04.s.s2.r.c: b=8 na case where dem make two triangles, so e support Gaeun statement.
x-m-h2-04.s.s2.r.d: E become c²−12c+95=0, wey no get real roots. No triangle fit make at all.
x-m-h2-04.s.s2.r.e: b=7 no dey inside condition “b bigger than 7.” E be case wey no relate to Gaeun statement.
x-m-h2-04.s.s2.r.f: E become c²−9c+32=0, wey no get real roots. No triangle fit make.
x-m-h2-04.s.s2.explain: By cosine rule, 49=b²+c²−bc, that is c²−bc+(b²−49)=0. For two different positive solutions, discriminant 196−3b² must be positive, and b>7, so b must be less than about 8.08. For b=9, 10, 12 no real roots dey, so no triangle fit make. b=5 and 7 dey outside condition b>7.
x-m-h2-04.s.s3.prompt: Answer Gaeun in one or two sentences. Use examples explain how many triangles get made depending on b value.
x-m-h2-04.s.s3.hint.0: Compare result for b=8 wey you find above with results for other values of b (for example 9, 10).
x-m-h2-04.s.s3.hint.1: Set up equation for c the same way, and count how many suitable positive c values dey.
x-m-h2-04.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You check with equation for c how many triangles dey for the b value you give?
x-m-h2-04.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You mention both case wey get two triangles and case wey get none?
x-m-h2-04.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You explain, even roughly, why triangles stop getting made as b gets bigger?
x-m-h2-04.s.s3.model.0: Not always. If b=8, c=3 and 5, so two dey; but if b=10, equation for c no get solution, so no triangle dey.
x-m-h2-04.s.s3.model.1: No. If b too big, no triangle fit make. If b=9 or 10, quadratic equation for c no get real roots, so e no work. Two only dey when b small pass 7, like b=8.

x-m-h2-05.title: 1, 2, 4, 8, … Wetin be next number?
x-m-h2-05.goal: See one rule wey you guess from first few terms break when new data show, and revise your judgment.
x-m-h2-05.material: If you mark n points on circle and connect every two points with straight line segment, circle divide into several regions. Mark points so no three line segments meet at one point. Call number of regions aₙ. (No need picture: with 1 point no segment dey, so 1 region; with 2 points one segment divide circle into two.)
x-m-h2-05.thinking.1: Revise your judgment with new data
x-m-h2-05.thinking.2: Explain the difference between guess and proof
x-m-h2-05.prereq.0: Meaning of sequence and its terms
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.prompt: Data go show one part at a time. At each step, choose prediction or judgment.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.hint.0: At each step, separate wetin you fit talk from data till now from wetin you no know yet.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.hint.1: When new data show, put dem beside your first prediction and compare whether e correct.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.0.info: When I count directly with 1, 2, 3, and 4 points, number of regions na 1, 2, 4, 8.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.0.ask: Wetin you predict the number of regions go be when 5 points dey?

x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.0.o.a: E go be 16. E keep doubling
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.0.r.a: If we look only the first four terms, doubling rule na the simplest guess.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.0.o.b: E go be 12. E increase by 4 each time
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.0.r.b: For 1, 2, 4, 8, the differences na 1, 2, 4, and dem keep getting bigger. Rule of adding 4 each time no match the data.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.0.o.c: E look like e go be 16, but before direct counting I no fit sure
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You dey think say guessing and checking na separate things.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.1.info: I mark 5 points and count directly, and e be 16.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.1.ask: Wetin you think when 6 points dey?
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.1.after: E fit reach fifth term, so your confidence don increase, but na still only evidence.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.1.o.a: E be 32. E fit work till 5, so doubling rule don confirm
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Because e fit till 5, you trust am more, but that alone no make you sure.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.1.o.b: E likely 32, but I no go sure till I count 6-point case directly
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You separate how strong the guess be from being sure.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.1.o.c: E fit less than 32, so I go count 6-point case directly
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You leave room say rule fit break and dey try test am.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.2.info: When I count 6-point case directly, e be 31. (Note: with 7 points e be 57.)
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.2.ask: Wetin you think about rule “aₙ=2ⁿ⁻¹ (2 to power n−1)”?
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.2.after: Sequence na 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 31, 57, so doubling rule no be rule for this sequence.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.2.o.a: For 6th term e be 31, so this rule no fit the sequence. Even if first few terms same, e no make am the same sequence.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You accept say one counterexample fit break a rule.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Only n=6 na exception, and the rest na 2ⁿ⁻¹
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.2.r.b: At n=7 e be 57, wey different from 2⁶=64, so more than one exception dey.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.2.o.c: E fit till 5, so dem must count 6th term wrong
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You no trust the result and try keep the rule. You fit check the counting again, but 57 no fit the rule too.
x-m-h2-05.s.s1.reflect: At first, doubling rule look likely, but new data (n=6) break am. Guess wey come from few terms na only evidence till e get confirmation, and to trust rule you need explanation why e hold for every n.
x-m-h2-05.s.s2.prompt: Write why you no fit fix one rule just because first few terms same, and wetin else you need before you believe say rule correct.
x-m-h2-05.s.s2.hint.0: Put number of regions 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 31 side by side with your first prediction.
x-m-h2-05.s.s2.hint.1: Think about how “I don check the rule” different from “I don explain the reason.”
x-m-h2-05.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You point out the exact value where rule break (n=6, 31)?
x-m-h2-05.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You separate “check more terms” from “explain reason”?
x-m-h2-05.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You say how you revise your first prediction?
x-m-h2-05.s.s2.model.0: Even though first five terms 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 match doubling rule, sixth term na 31, so rule break. No fix a rule by looking at only few terms; you need reason (proof) why e hold for every n.
x-m-h2-05.s.s2.model.1: Checking some terms na evidence, no be certainty. This sequence na 31 when n=6, so rule of powers of 2 wrong. To trust rule, you must fit explain why e hold for all terms.

x-m-h2-06.title: Check solution wey find general term from sum of sequence
x-m-h2-06.goal: Find and correct problem in solution wey find general term from sum Sₙ of sequence, and find the condition yourself wey make am fit write as one formula.
x-m-h2-06.material: This na Seoa solution for finding general term when sum Sₙ of first n terms for sequence {aₙ} na Sₙ = n² + 2n + 1. (Read Sₙ as “S sub n”, aₙ as “a sub n”, and Sₙ₋₁ as “S sub n minus 1”.)
x-m-h2-06.thinking.1: Separate formulas wey apply for different ranges
x-m-h2-06.prereq.0: Meaning of sum Sₙ and general term aₙ of sequence
x-m-h2-06.s.s1.prompt: Choose line for Seoa solution wey get problem. (If several lines in order get problem, you fit choose only one.)
x-m-h2-06.s.s1.hint.0: Compare whether condition (range for n) at start of each line same as range for final conclusion.
x-m-h2-06.s.s1.hint.1: Find first term a₁ directly from definition of Sₙ, and compare am with value for line 5.
x-m-h2-06.s.s1.line.3: So for all natural numbers n, aₙ = 2n + 1
x-m-h2-06.s.s1.explain: Line 4 na the problem. Line 1 talk n≥2, so aₙ=2n+1 na formula we get only for n≥2. We must find first term separately: a₁=S₁=1+2+1=4, wey different from 2·1+1=3. So a₁=3 for line 5 wrong too.
x-m-h2-06.s.s2.prompt: Write correct general term and explain wetin Seoa miss.
x-m-h2-06.s.s2.hint.0: Formula to find a₁ defined different from aₙ=Sₙ−Sₙ₋₁. Remember the meaning of first term.
x-m-h2-06.s.s2.hint.1: Compare value of 2n+1 when n=1 with value of S₁.
x-m-h2-06.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You find a₁ from S₁, instead of aₙ=Sₙ−Sₙ₋₁?
x-m-h2-06.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You say we gats check whether formula we find for n≥2 too work for n=1?
x-m-h2-06.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You write general term as two cases, instead of one formula?
x-m-h2-06.s.s2.model.0: a₁=S₁=4, and for n≥2, aₙ=2n+1. Seoa no check whether formula wey e find for n≥2 too work for n=1. Putting n=1 gives 3, wey different from a₁=4.
x-m-h2-06.s.s2.model.1: General term must write in two parts: a₁=4, and aₙ=2n+1 (n≥2). S₁=4, but putting n=1 inside 2n+1 gives 3, so dem no equal. We must find first term separately.
x-m-h2-06.s.s3.prompt: For Sₙ = p·n² + q·n + r (p, q, r na integers, p≠0), find three different (p, q, r) wey value from putting n=1 inside formula we find for n≥2 equal a₁, so general term fit write as one formula.
x-m-h2-06.s.s3.hint.0: For Sₙ=pn²+qn+r, write Sₙ−Sₙ₋₁ for n≥2 using p and q.
x-m-h2-06.s.s3.hint.1: Compare value from putting n=1 inside that formula with S₁=p+q+r.
x-m-h2-06.s.s3.ok.c1: p na integer wey no be 0.
x-m-h2-06.s.s3.fail.c1: p, q, r na integers and p must no be 0.
x-m-h2-06.s.s3.ok.c2: Value from formula we find for n≥2 when n=1 equal a₁=S₁.
x-m-h2-06.s.s3.fail.c2: Value p+q from formula p(2n−1)+q wey we find for n≥2 no equal S₁=p+q+r. (n=1)

x-m-h2-07.title: ∞−∞ equal 0? Check the claims from two friends
x-m-h2-07.goal: Use numerical calculations test two claims, explain where intuitive reasoning wrong, then find limit using algebra.
x-m-h2-07.material: Minsu talk say, “As x dey become endlessly big, √(x²+x) dey close to x, so √(x²+x) − x dey close to 0.” Seoa talk say, “E no dey close to 0; e dey close to some positive number.” How to read: √(x²+x) na root of x squared plus x, and “x dey become endlessly big” na x→∞.
x-m-h2-07.prereq.0: Meaning of limit as x dey become endlessly big
x-m-h2-07.s.s1.prompt: You fit use calculator. Choose three integers x wey at least 100, calculate √(x²+x) − x, round am to 3 decimal places, and enter as (x, value). Entering 3 different x values complete am. (If Minsu claim correct, value suppose dey closer to 0 as x bigger.)
x-m-h2-07.s.s1.hint.0: Put x=100 and x=1000 inside √(x²+x)−x and calculate.
x-m-h2-07.s.s1.hint.1: Make x bigger again and observe which direction the value move.
x-m-h2-07.s.s1.fail.c1: x must be integer at least 100.
x-m-h2-07.s.s1.ok.c2: The value you enter match calculated √(x²+x)−x.
x-m-h2-07.s.s1.fail.c2: The value you enter differ from calculated result. Recalculate √(x²+x)−x and round to 3 decimal places.
x-m-h2-07.s.s1.explain: For x=100, value about 0.4988; x=1000, about 0.49988; x=10000, about 0.49999. Even as x grow, e no go near 0; e stay around 0.5.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.prompt: From calculation, whose statement get better support, Minsu or Seoa? Choose best explanation.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.hint.0: Put calculated values for the 3 x values side by side and see what happen as x increase.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.hint.1: Separate "gets close" about ratio from "gets close" about difference.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.o.a: Seoa statement get support. Difference gather around a value wey no be 0.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.r.a: Even when x bigger, value no move near 0.5, so that evidence against claim say e be 0.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.o.b: Minsu correct. Ratio dey approach 1, so difference also approach 0.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.r.b: Ratio approaching 1 no mean difference approaching 0. For example, ratio x/(x+0.5) approach 1 but difference always 0.5.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.o.c: Minsu correct. Value greater than 0 na calculator error.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.r.c: When you change x and values gather around same value near 0.5, hard to call am error.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.o.d: Cannot tell either way. Calculation no tell anything.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.r.d: Numbers no prove the limit, but dem give evidence against claim of 0.
x-m-h2-07.s.s2.explain: Calculated values gather near 0.5 as x grows, so Seoa statement get support. But numbers na evidence only; to find exact value, transform expression.
x-m-h2-07.s.s3.prompt: Explain why Minsu reasoning "√(x²+x) approaches x, so difference 0" wrong, and find limit by transforming.
x-m-h2-07.s.s3.hint.0: Write what numerator become when multiply and divide √(x²+x)−x by √(x²+x)+x.
x-m-h2-07.s.s3.hint.1: Divide numerator and denominator by x, then see what value each part approach as x grows without limit.
x-m-h2-07.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You separate two values getting close from their difference going to 0?
x-m-h2-07.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did your transformation make expression ready for finding limit?
x-m-h2-07.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Does calculated value 0.4999… match limit you find?
x-m-h2-07.s.s3.model.0: Getting close to x means ratio get close to 1, no be difference 0. Rationalizing numerator gives x/(√(x²+x)+x)=1/(√(1+1/x)+1); as x→∞, result 1/2.
x-m-h2-07.s.s3.model.1: Even if √(x²+x) look like x, there still be difference, so no change it to x−x=0. Multiply top and bottom by conjugate √(x²+x)+x gives x/(√(x²+x)+x), whose limit na 0.5 (=1/2).

x-m-h2-08.title: From Average Speed to Instantaneous Speed
x-m-h2-08.goal: Make interval smaller and see what value average speed approach; organize meaning of instantaneous speed.
x-m-h2-08.material: Ball rolling down slope travels s(t)=t² meters in t seconds. Find speed "at that moment" t=1 second. But speed na distance÷time; at an instant elapsed time 0, so division seem impossible.
x-m-h2-08.thinking.2: Organize meaning of instantaneous rate of change
x-m-h2-08.prereq.0: Meaning of average rate of change (average speed)
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.prompt: Info come out one piece at a time. At each step, choose judgment.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.hint.0: From revealed information, write interval length and average speed side by side.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.hint.1: Compare your prediction with new result; if different, think what you miss.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.0.info: Average speed over [1,3] seconds na (9−1)÷2=4 m/s. Interval starts at 1 and ends at 3.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.0.ask: What you conclude about speed exactly at t=1 second?
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.0.after: Long interval means speed changes during it, so average differs from speed at one instant. Make interval shorter.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.0.o.a: It is 4 m/s. Average speed na speed at that moment.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.0.r.a: If speed change during interval, no say average equal speed at starting instant.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Cannot say yet. Need average speed over shorter intervals starting at 1 second too.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Instead of using one long interval to settle instant speed, check with shorter intervals.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Cannot know. At an instant time is 0, so speed cannot be defined.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Cannot divide directly over zero time, but we fit approach it with short intervals. The time interval no be 0.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.1.ask: If interval shrink smaller, for example [1, 1.01] and [1, 1.001], what happen to average speed?
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.1.after: [1, 1.01] gives (1.0201−1)÷0.01=2.01; [1, 1.001] gives 2.001. Numerator and denominator approach 0, but ratio gather near 2.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.1.o.a: It approaches 0 because interval length approaches 0.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You only look at interval length. Distance traveled also gets small, so check ratio.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.1.r.b: As interval shrink from [1, 1.5] to [1, 1.1], average speed drop from 2.5 to 2.1.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You guess value from average speed trend 3, 2.5, 2.1.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.2.info: In general average speed over [1, 1+h] is ((1+h)²−1)÷h=2+h, where h≠0.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.2.ask: As h approaches 0 but is not 0, how should we define speed at t=1 second?
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.2.after: Instant speed na value 2 that average speed 2+h approach as h→0. This called derivative at t=1.
x-m-h2-08.s.s1.st.2.o.a: It is 2+h; it depends on h.

x-m-h2-10.title: Make probability for sum of two dice
x-m-h2-10.goal: Count cases to build event meeting condition, explain why probabilities same, and judge common misconception.
x-m-h2-10.material: Roll 2 distinct dice (red and blue) once; call sum s. There are 36 equally likely outcomes. For example sum 2 has only one: (red 1, blue 1).
x-m-h2-10.s.s1.prompt: Find 2 different s values where probability of sum s is exactly 1/9 (=4/36). s integer from 2 to 12.

x-m-h2-10.s.s1.ok.c2: There are 4 cases with sum s, so probability 4/36=1/9.
x-m-h2-10.s.s1.fail.c2: Number of cases for sum s no be 4. List and count ordered pairs making s.
x-m-h2-10.s.s1.explain: Sum 5 outcomes: (1,4),(2,3),(3,2),(4,1), total 4. Sum 9 outcomes: (3,6),(4,5),(5,4),(6,3), also 4; probabilities both 4/36=1/9.

x-m-h2-10.s.s1.because.selfAssess.1: You explain sameness by structure, no be coincidence?
x-m-h2-10.s.s1.because.selfAssess.2: You say how it differ from sum 7 (6 ways)?
x-m-h2-10.s.s1.because.model.0: Sum 5 cases na 4 pairs (1,4),(2,3),(3,2),(4,1); sum 9 has 4 too: (3,6),(4,5),(5,4),(6,3). If number x turns into 7−x, pairs match each other; sums symmetric around 7, so counts same.
x-m-h2-10.s.s1.because.model.1: 5 and 9 are both 2 away from 7, symmetric. Each get 4 cases (4/36), so probabilities equal.
x-m-h2-10.s.s2.prompt: Student says probability sum 2 same as sum 3, both only one way like 1+1 and 1+2. What best identify error?
x-m-h2-10.s.s2.hint.0: List all ordered (red,blue) pairs giving sums 2 and 3.

x-m-h2-10.s.s2.o.c: Sum 3 has 2 ways (1,2),(2,1); sum 2 only one (1,1).
x-m-h2-10.s.s2.r.c: Key point: swapping numbers on different dice gives different outcomes.
x-m-h2-10.s.s2.o.d: Sum 2 even and sum 3 odd, so probabilities differ.

x-m-h2-09.s.s1.fail.c1: a and b must be integers.
x-m-h2-09.title: If derivative at a point is 0, is it always an extremum?
x-m-h2-09.goal: Make counterexample to claim "derivative 0 means extremum" and organize conditions needed for extremum.
x-m-h2-09.material: Student says, "For cubic f(x)=x³+ax²+bx, if f'(c)=0, there is always local maximum or minimum at x=c." (f' is derivative, f'(x)=3x²+2ax+b. Extremum is where function changes increasing to decreasing or reverse.)
x-m-h2-09.prereq.0: Meaning of derivative and differentiating polynomials
x-m-h2-09.s.s1.prompt: Find 3 different integer pairs a,b where f has some c with f'(c)=0 but no extremum (it never decreases on any interval), as counterexamples.
x-m-h2-09.s.s1.hint.0: Picture f'(x)=3x²+2ax+b (upward parabola). For f to have extremum, f' sign must change.
x-m-h2-09.s.s1.hint.1: How must parabola meet x-axis so f'(c)=0 but sign does not change?
x-m-h2-09.s.s1.ok.c2: f'(x)=3x²+2ax+b tangent to x-axis. Some c has f'(c)=0, but sign no change.
x-m-h2-09.s.s1.fail.c2: Discriminant 4a²−12b of f' no be 0. If positive, f' changes sign and extremum; if negative, no c with f'(c)=0. If discriminant =0 and c=−a/3, the root does not cross. Discriminant is 0, and example a=0 gives 3(x+0/3)². The coefficient 2a is present too.
x-m-h2-09.s.s1.explain: If f'(x)=3x²+2ax+b tangent to x-axis (discriminant 4a²−12b=0, meaning a²=3b), then f'(x)=3(x+a/3)²≥0. Though f'=0 at one point, f keeps increasing. Example a=0,b=0 gives f=x³ and f'(0)=0, but no extremum.
x-m-h2-09.s.s2.prompt: For functions you made, f'(c)=0 but no extremum. What condition best for extremum?
x-m-h2-09.s.s2.hint.0: Check sign of f'(x) to left and right of c for your example.
x-m-h2-09.s.s2.hint.1: Compare meaning of extremum (change increasing/decreasing) with each option.
x-m-h2-09.s.s2.o.a: f'(c)=0 and sign of f' changes on both sides of c
x-m-h2-09.s.s2.r.a: You point out besides f'(c)=0, increasing/decreasing must switch.
x-m-h2-09.s.s2.o.b: If f'(c)=0, it always extremum regardless of sign.
x-m-h2-09.s.s2.r.b: Earlier example f=x³ had f'(0)=0 but no extremum.
x-m-h2-09.s.s2.o.c: f'(c)=0 and f(c) must also be 0.
x-m-h2-09.s.s2.r.c: f(c) value no relate to extremum. For f=x³+1, f'(0)=0 and f(0)=1, but no extremum.
x-m-h2-09.s.s2.r.d: If f'(c)>0, tangent slope positive, so function increasing; not an extremum candidate.
x-m-h2-09.s.s2.explain: For c to be extremum, f'(c)=0 and f' sign change across c. f'(c)=0 alone only necessary for candidate.
